lessons.title: Division as sharing
lessons.objective: Share a number of things equally.

introduce.text: Division means sharing equally. Here are 12 laddoos. Everyone must get the same number.
introduce.speech: Division means sharing equally. Here are 12 laddoos. Everyone must get the same number.

introduce.text: We share 12 laddoos among 3 children. We write it as 12 ÷ 3. The sign ÷ means shared equally among.
introduce.speech: We share 12 laddoos among 3 children. We write it as 12 divided by 3. The sign divided by means shared equally among.

demonstrate.text: Give one laddoo at a time to each of the 3 children until all 12 are given. Each child gets 4.
demonstrate.speech: Give one laddoo at a time to each of the 3 children until all 12 are given. Each child gets 4.

demonstrate.text: Each child has 4 laddoos, so 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Check: 3 x 4 = 12.
demonstrate.speech: Each child has 4 laddoos, so 12 divided by 3 equals 4. Check: 3 times 4 equals 12.

guided.prompt: 15 toffees are shared equally among 3 children. How many does each child get?
guided.speech: 15 toffees are shared equally among 3 children. How many does each child get?

Ask: 3 x what makes 15? Count in 3s up to 15.

wrong_feedback.12: 12 is 15 - 3. Sharing is not taking away. Ask how many each one gets.
wrong_feedback.3: 3 is the number you share among, not what each one gets.

lessons.title: Multiplication and division fact families
lessons.objective: Use one multiplication fact to find a division fact.

introduce.text: One multiplication fact can give us division facts. Look at 3 groups of 4. That is 3 x 4 = 12.
introduce.speech: One multiplication fact can give us division facts. Look at 3 groups of 4. That is 3 times 4 equals 12.

introduce.text: The same three numbers make a fact family: 3 x 4 = 12, 4 x 3 = 12, 12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
introduce.speech: The same three numbers make a fact family: 3 times 4 equals 12, 4 times 3 equals 12, 12 divided by 4 equals 3 and 12 divided by 3 equals 4.

demonstrate.text: Start with 12 mangoes in 3 rows of 4. Share them into rows of 4 and you get 3 rows. So 12 ÷ 4 = 3.
demonstrate.speech: Start with 12 mangoes in 3 rows of 4. Share them into rows of 4 and you get 3 rows. So 12 divided by 4 equals 3.

demonstrate.text: Share the same 12 mangoes into 4 rows of 3 and you get 3 in each row. So 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
demonstrate.speech: Share the same 12 mangoes into 4 rows of 3 and you get 3 in each row. So 12 divided by 3 equals 4.

guided.speech: 6 times 3 equals 18, so 18 divided by 3 equals ?
hints: Division undoes multiplication. Look at the fact 6 x 3 = 18.
18 ÷ 3 asks: 3 times what makes 18? Use the fact above.

wrong_feedback.18: 18 is the whole number we are dividing, not the answer.
wrong_feedback.9: 9 is 6 + 3. Division undoes multiplication, it does not add.

guided.speech: 4 times what equals 28
hints: This is a missing number. A division fact can find it: 28 ÷ 4.
Count in 4s until you reach 28. How many jumps?

practice.speech: 5 times 4 equals 20, so 20 divided by 4 equals ?
hints: Division undoes multiplication. Look at the fact 5 x 4 = 20.
20 ÷ 4 asks: 4 times what makes 20? Use the fact above.

wrong_feedback.20: 20 is the whole number we are dividing, not the answer.
wrong_feedback.9: 9 is 5 + 4. Division undoes multiplication, it does not add.

practice.speech: 45 divided by 5 equals ?
hints: Use the multiplication family. 5 times what makes 45?
Count in 5s up to 45 and count the jumps.

wrong_feedback.45: 45 is the number we start with, not the answer.
wrong_feedback.40: 40 is 45 - 5. This is division, not subtraction.

practice.speech: Which fact is in the same family as 8 times 3 equals 24?
hints: A family fact uses the same three numbers. Try each one with the multiplication fact.

lessons.title: Halves, quarters and thirds
lessons.objective: Name equal parts of a whole as halves, quarters and thirds.

introduce.text: Equal parts are all the same size. A roti cut into 2 equal parts has 2 pieces that are the same size.
introduce.speech: Equal parts are all the same size. A roti cut into 2 equal parts has 2 pieces that are the same size.

introduce.text: 2 equal parts are halves. 3 equal parts are thirds. 4 equal parts are quarters. One part is one half, one third or one quarter.
introduce.speech: 2 equal parts are halves. 3 equal parts are thirds. 4 equal parts are quarters. One part is one half, one third or one quarter.

visual.glyph: ½ = 1 of 2 parts   ⅓ = 1 of 3   ¼ = 1 of 4

demonstrate.text: Here are 8 mangoes shared into 2 equal groups of 4. Each group is one half of the mangoes. Half of 8 is 4.
demonstrate.speech: Here are 8 mangoes shared into 2 equal groups of 4. Each group is one half of the mangoes. Half of 8 is 4.

demonstrate.text: Share the 8 mangoes into 4 equal groups of 2. Each group is one quarter. A quarter of 8 is 2.

lessons.title: Money and change
lessons.objective: Add prices and find change in rupees.

introduce.text: Change is the money you get back. You give more money than the price. The extra comes back to you.
introduce.speech: Change is the money you get back. You give more money than the price. The extra comes back to you.

introduce.text: To find change, take the price away from the money you give. We use subtraction.
introduce.speech: To find change, take the price away from the money you give. We use subtraction.

demonstrate.text: Here are 20 coins to pay with. The price is 7, so take 7 coins away.
demonstrate.speech: Here are 20 coins to pay with. The price is 7, so take 7 coins away.

demonstrate.text: 13 coins are left. So the change is 20 - 7 = ₹13.

lessons.title: Time to five minutes
lessons.objective: Tell the time to five minutes from a clock described in words.

introduce.text: A clock has a short hand and a long hand. The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.
introduce.speech: A clock has a short hand and a long hand. The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.

visual.glyph: short hand = hour   long hand = minutes

introduce.text: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. When the long hand is on 1 it is 5 minutes, on 2 it is 10, on 3 it is 15 and on 6 it is 30. On 12 it is o'clock.
introduce.speech: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. When the long hand is on 1 it is 5 minutes, on 2 it is 10, on 3 it is 15 and on 6 it is 30. On 12 it is o'clock.

demonstrate.text: Count in fives round the clock to read the long hand: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.

lessons.title: Length and mass
lessons.objective: Choose a sensible unit and compare lengths and masses.

introduce.text: We measure length in centimetres (cm) for small things like a pencil, and in metres (m) for big things like a door or a room. 1 m = 100 cm.
introduce.speech: We measure length in centimetres  for small things like a pencil, and in metres  for big things like a door or a room. 1 metres equals 100 centimetres.

introduce.text: We measure mass in grams (g) for light things like an egg, and in kilograms (kg) for heavy things like a bag of rice. 1 kg = 1000 g.
introduce.speech: We measure mass in grams  for light things like an egg, and in kilograms  for heavy things like a bag of rice. 1 kilograms equals 1000 grams.

demonstrate.text: A metre stick is 100 centimetres long. So 2 m is 200 cm and 3 m is 300 cm.
demonstrate.speech: A metre stick is 100 centimetres long. So 2 metres is 200 centimetres and 3 metres is 300 centimetres.

demonstrate.text: A packet of sugar can be 1 kg, which is 1000 g. So 2 kg is 2000 g. To compare, change both to the same unit.
demonstrate.speech: A packet of sugar can be 1 kilograms, which is 1000 grams. So 2 kilograms is 2000 grams. To compare, change both to the same unit.

guided.prompt: Which unit is best to measure the length of a classroom?
guided.speech: Which unit is best to measure the length of a classroom?
hints: A classroom is big. Which unit is for big lengths?
Use metres for long distances.

wrong_feedback.centimetres (cm): A classroom is very long, so centimetres would give a huge number.

guided.explanation: A classroom is measured in metres.

guided.prompt: Which unit is best to measure the mass of an egg?
guided.speech: Which unit is best to measure the mass of an egg?
hints: An egg is light. Which unit is for light things?

wrong_feedback.kilograms (kg): An egg is very light, so kilograms would be too big.

guided.explanation: An egg is measured in grams.

lessons.title: Word problems and reasoning
lessons.objective: Choose the right operation to solve a short story problem.

introduce.text: To solve a story, first decide what is happening. Put together means add. Take away means subtract.
introduce.speech: To solve a story, first decide what is happening. Put together means add. Take away means subtract.

introduce.text: Equal groups means multiply. Sharing equally means divide. Read the story and pick the operation.
introduce.speech: Equal groups means multiply. Sharing equally means divide. Read the story and pick the operation.

demonstrate.text: The story: 3 bags have 4 apples each. The bags are equal groups, so multiply: 3 x 4.
demonstrate.speech: The story: 3 bags have 4 apples each. The bags are equal groups, so multiply: 3 times 4.

demonstrate.text: 3 x 4 = 12, so there are 12 apples in all.
demonstrate.speech: 3 times 4 equals 12, so there are 12 apples in all.

guided.prompt: 24 sweets are shared equally among 6 children. Which sum finds how many each child gets?
guided.speech: 24 sweets are shared equally among 6 children. Which sum finds how many each child gets?

Add to put together, subtract to take away, multiply for equal groups, divide to share.
